items.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012
items.q: I played for a vocal jazz group in college. A professor named Robert Porter, a great professor out at the University of Wisconsin Milwaukee.

ctx.x: Yeah. You probably get a sense fairly quickly in working with a particular singer like I need to lead this person a little bit or not be too — my substitutions, watch out for them. Right.

Um hum. Well I look to people like Nelson Riddle, Axle Stordahl and even people with film scores like Erich Korngold, you just listen to what’s going on behind the action. And you know how much you can get away with almost immediately if you’re doing stuff and they get lost. But that rarely happens. I mean usually they can follow. Because they’re used to playing with something — in other words I will stray from the standard changes after a chorus or two. And the vocalists welcome that. They actually are happy…

audited the class. I did it because I just wanted to meet girls. But I was playing with them and I learned, again, less is more, don’t try to overplay them, don’t try to upstage them. Just do your thing. If they look good you look good. And again, a lot of times I’ll actually take my hands completely off the keys and I’ll allow some silence. Because if there’s a vocal person, that’s a brave thing to do. I know that as a heavy metal singer too. Getting up and singing in front of a crowd is a brave thing to do. You…
